title: Benny Harris hears him and gets him into Earl Hines's band
summary: When Hines played Detroit, trumpeter Benny Harris told Budd Johnson and Scoops Carey about Nicholas, who was hired for his tone and reading.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: But that's where Benny Harris heard me, you know, when Earl Hines came to town and he came in the club and he immediately told Budd Johnson and Scoops Carey and that's how I was hired. Benny Harris, the trumpet player. Yeah. He passed on. But he was playin' like Dizzy then. You know he was...he really had the feeling of Dizzy and everybody was crazy about him in the band. In fact, everybody was crazy about Little Benny; we called him "Little Benny". And he got me in the band because I had a tone. I wasn't a great soloist, but I could read and I had a tone. And that's how that started. Then when I got in there, boy, it was really something, because Earl Hines's music was very, very, very difficult. And especially for the reed section.
Was he just passing through town then?
I don't know. I think they
were playin' a dance and they were around there for two or three days and I think they had a dance and then they laid over a couple of days.
Who did you replace in this band?
I'm tryin' to think who I replaced...umum. I can't think of that fella's name.
